summary: This is the most heterogeneous run in the batch — a single session that touches customer-support refunds, contact management, flight and hotel bookings, an airline profile, a promo-code application, and a reminder, across at least six different people. It opens on the actual request: a supplemental refund on Nina Patel's order ORD-9497C0 for the OXO Salad Spinner, processed and detailed at T1. From there it sprawls: James Park's profile (T2, T8), contacts Daniel Mercer and Jordan Kim (T3–T4), the refund restated (T5), Sofia Martinez's flight + profile (T6–T7), a Maya Chen hotel (T9), Jordan Kim's airline profile + fare math (T10), Evan Parker's promo cart (T11), a reminder plus a block of 'Restated' recalls (T12), and a ten-item recap (T13). Recall traps land on T5, T7, T11, T12, all COMPLY: the refund, the HATHAT booking, the Jordan Kim contact, and a whole bundle of restated flight/fare/hotel/promo facts are pulled from working memory. The only FAIL sub-checks are exact-token mismatches — the goodwill-credit restatement on T5 and the promo discount recalled as $11 rather than $11.85 on T12 — not lost memory. T12 is the densest recall turn, re-serving four prior results at once.
